age.evidence: male and female adolescent rats were given either 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle on postnatal day (P) 35 and 45 ... on approximately P125 and P132, these animals were again administered 1 mg/kg psilocybin; A total of 13 adult ( > P100) female Long Evans rats

sex.evidence: A total of 65 (33 female, 32 male) Long Evans rats ... A total of 13 adult ( > P100) female Long Evans rats were purchased

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/ml) or distilled water vehicle was administered by gavage of 1 ml/kg. ... given either 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle on postnatal day (P) 35 and 45 ... on approximately P125 and P132, these animals were again administered 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle (order counterbalanced)

group_housing.evidence: Animals received identifying foot tattoos and were pairhoused on P30. ... All animals were pairhoused

day_night_flipped.evidence: They were kept on a 12 h light/dark cycle (on at 0700 h) with all experiments occurring during the light cycle (between 0900 and 1400 h).

assays.assay_description: 30-min video recording immediately after gavage of 1 mg/kg psilocybin or water vehicle; adolescents (P35, P45) in a ~33x20x15 cm cage with transparent lid, adults (>P125, and estrous-study females in diestrus/proestrus) in a ~56 cm diameter x 30 cm polycarbonate tube. HTRs coded by two blinded observers. Includes adolescent, adult re-exposure and estrous-phase cohorts.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/ml) or distilled water vehicle was administered by gavage of 1 ml/kg.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowing for age-appropriate horizontal and vertical movement and facilitating video recording

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the recording cage/tube during the 30-min session

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the recording cage/tube during the 30-min session

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately after gavage, adolescents were placed into a ~33 cm × 20 cm x 15 cm cage with a transparent lid and video recorded for 30-min.

sample_size.evidence: P35, n = 10-11/treatment/sex ... P45, n = 10-11/treatment/sex ... adulthood ( > P125, n = 7-10/treatment/sex); estrous study n = 11-13/treatment/phase (13 females)

outcomes.summary: 1 mg/kg intragastric psilocybin increased head twitches in adult rats but not in adolescents (P35, P45). Adult females twitched more than adult males; adolescent pre-exposure did not alter adult HTR; adult females in diestrus showed more psilocybin-induced HTRs than in proestrus.
outcomes.statistics: Three-way ANOVA: age x sex x treatment F(2,106)=7.30, p=0.001; age x treatment F(2,106)=30.26, p<0.0001; sex x treatment F(1,106)=6.62, p=0.012; age x sex F(2,106)=12.51, p<0.0001; sex F(1,106)=11.03, p=0.001; treatment F(1,106)=66.25, p<0.0001; age F(2,106)=61.37, p<0.0001; post hoc adult females p<0.0001, adult males p=0.0024; adult F vs M psilocybin p<0.0001. Adult re-exposure: sex F(1,54)=8.99, p=0.0041. Estrous: treatment F(1,45)=32.83, p<0.0001; stage F(1,45)=8.396, p=0.0058; proestrus p=0.0057, diestrus p=0.0001, diestrus vs proestrus p=0.035.
outcomes.evidence: compared to vehicle, psilocybin treatment increased head twitch responses in adult females (p < 0.0001) and adult males (p = 0.0024), but did not increase head twitches in either P35 or P45 animals.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Head twitch responses ... briefly defined by a rapid side-to-side and rotational motion of the head or entire body (single count measure)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: A time course of head twitch responses in adult subjects showed an onset of behavioral effects of psilocybin within 5 min ... across the 30-min recording period (Supplemental Fig. S2).

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

B5_social.evidence: No social component; animals recorded individually

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Each video recording was coded by two observers, blind to treatment

E1_environment_type.evidence: placed into a ~33 cm × 20 cm x 15 cm cage with a transparent lid ... a large polycarbonate tube ~56 cm diameter x 30 cm height

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in recording cage/tube

E6_spatial.evidence: Single cage or tube without compartments

E7_social_context.evidence: Animals placed individually into the recording enclosure

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described in the recording enclosure

D1_continuity.evidence: HTR assessed on P35, P45 and approximately P125 and P132; estrous study: a series of 4 tests separated by at least 1 week

D3_recording_days.evidence: Adolescent cohort: P35, P45, ~P125, ~P132 (4 days); estrous cohort: 4 tests per animal

D5_followup.evidence: adult HTR at approximately P125/P132 after adolescent psilocybin on P35/P45; estrous vehicle sessions separated by at least 1 week from psilocybin sessions

assays.assay_description: 10-min test on P90/91 in a circular maze (40 inch diameter) with two open stretches and two closed arms (12-inch walls), ~1000 lux; Any-Maze measured time in and entries into open arms. Tests lasting effects of adolescent psilocybin.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/ml) or distilled water vehicle was administered by gavage of 1 ml/kg (on P35/P45)

setup_habituation.evidence: Subjects were kept in their home cages for 15 min prior to the test to allow for habituation to the testing room. (room acclimation only, not apparatus habituation)

setup_restrain.evidence: subjects were placed in the center of one of the closed arms and were recorded for 10 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in maze during 10-min test

water_restriction.evidence: No water in maze during 10-min test

time_to_assay.evidence: Animals treated with psilocybin or vehicle on P35 and P45 ... completed elevated zero maze testing on P90/91

sample_size.evidence: n = 10-11/treatment/sex/age; A total of 65 (33 female, 32 male) Long Evans rats

outcomes.summary: Adolescent psilocybin exposure (P35 or P45) did not alter adult percentage time in open areas or open-area entries in the elevated zero maze; no sex effects.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA found no significant effects of sex or treatment, nor their interaction (no F values reported).
outcomes.evidence: Two-way ANOVA of the percentage of time spent in the open areas of the maze (Fig. 3A) found no significant effects of sex or treatment, nor their interaction. In addition, no significant effects of sex or treatment were found on the number of entries into the open areas (Fig. 3B).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Any-Maze video analysis software (v4.99) was used to calculate total time spent in the open arms as well as total entries into the open arms.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Any-Maze video analysis software (v4.99) — on SCORE-0 list

E1_environment_type.evidence: circular testing apparatus (diameter = 40 inches) with two open stretches of maze and two 'closed arms'

E2_shelter.evidence: Closed arms are part of apparatus design, not a shelter per rubric

E6_spatial.evidence: Zero maze arms are continuous track sections, treated like EPM per rubric

E7_social_context.evidence: subjects were placed in the center of one of the closed arms

D1_continuity.evidence: completed elevated zero maze testing on P90/91

D5_followup.evidence: EZM on P90/91, ~45 days after last adolescent dose on P45

assays.assay_description: Operant lever-press task in Med Associates chambers under food restriction (1-h sessions, 30 trials/day): shaping, acquisition (80%/20% reward probability, criterion 24/30 correct two days in a row), then reversal of contingencies for up to 21 days; days to criterion analysed by Cox proportional hazards.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/ml) or distilled water vehicle was administered by gavage of 1 ml/kg (on P35/P45)

setup_habituation.evidence: Subjects started with a shaping phase where they established that pressing the levers resulted in a sugar pellet reward.

setup_restrain.evidence: standard operant chambers (Med Associates, St Albans, VT); free movement

food_restriction.evidence: all food was removed from each cage. After this point, subjects were fed once per day with 3.5 % of their free-feeding body weight in grams

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in operant chamber

time_to_assay.evidence: Beginning on P93, these animals then underwent training and testing for probabilistic spatial reversal learning

sample_size.evidence: animals treated with psilocybin or vehicle on P35 and P45 (n = 10-11/treatment/sex/age)

outcomes.summary: Adolescent psilocybin exposure did not alter rate of initial acquisition or rate of reversal learning in adulthood; no sex effects.
outcomes.statistics: Cox Proportional Hazard Model found no significant differences due to subject sex, treatment, nor their interaction (no test statistics reported).
outcomes.evidence: The rate of initial acquisition ... found no significant differences due to subject sex, treatment, nor their interaction ... Survival analysis of the rate of reversal learning was conducted, which again found no effect of sex, treatment, or their interaction

B1_num_measures.evidence: rate of initial acquisition; rate of reversal learning (days to criterion); subjects who never achieved acquisition after reversal were noted

B4_ethological.evidence: Lever pressing is operant, not ethological

B6_cognitive.evidence: probabilistic spatial reversal learning, to determine if adolescent treatment with psilocybin affected adult behavioral flexibility

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates operant chambers — on SCORE-0 list

E1_environment_type.evidence: standard operant chambers (Med Associates, St Albans, VT)

E8_food_water.evidence: pressing the levers resulted in a sugar pellet reward

D1_continuity.evidence: daily sessions (30 trials per day) through acquisition and reversal

D3_recording_days.evidence: shaping (≥2 days per lever), acquisition (criterion two days in a row), reversal up to 21 days; exact count not stated

D5_followup.evidence: PRL beginning P93, ~48 days after last adolescent dose

judge_notes: Three assays retained (HTR, EZM, PRL), all candidates agreed on granularity; adolescent, adult re-exposure, and estrous HTR cohorts merged into one HTR assay.
HTR B1 set to 1 measure (score 0): time course is temporal dynamics (B2=1), not a separate measure; gemma's score 1 with value '1' was inconsistent.
HTR D3 set to 2-7 days: each animal was recorded on at most 4 days (P35, P45, ~P125, ~P132; or 4 estrous tests); overrode two candidates who summed across cohorts.
HTR D2 = 30 min (score 1); gemma's '<15 min' contradicted its own evidence.
EZM setup_habituation set to not_reported: paper only describes 15-min testing-room acclimation, which the rubric excludes.
EZM B1 score corrected to 1 (2 measures); EZM and PRL D5 = Yes since testing occurred weeks after adolescent dosing (gemma's No overridden).
PRL D3 kept at modal 8-14 (exact number of sessions not reported).
time_to_assay minutes recomputed from P45 (last adolescent dose) to P90 (EZM) and P93 (PRL).
Sex n_female = 46 (33 adolescent-study + 13 estrous-study females); dosing schedule 'repeated' since animals received up to 2 psilocybin doses.
